notes: Provisional: PR #18 is an open draft, not merged; numbers may change before publication.
Data: Microcosm UK 2024-25 (microcosm-uk-2024-25-national-20261107T020434Z-eeb6093e), simulated for 2026 with PolicyEngine-UK.

Central scenario: 7% of employees displaced in proportion to occupational AI exposure (C-AIOE), survivors' wages up 2.6% on average, interest and dividend income up 39.8% (+0.4pp return); displaced workers lose a full year of earnings.
Exchequer cost is the fall in the government balance: income tax, employee and employer NI, and benefits; it counts no corporation tax. A negative cost is a net gain.
Poverty is the absolute line (frozen at baseline) before housing costs unless stated; Gini changes are in points (x100).

Draw counts differ: headline 50 draws; take-up, JSA and wage-cut variants 20 draws paired with seeds 0-19 of the central run (central on those seeds costs £7.2bn); low and high scenarios one draw (seed 0); job-loss cost per pound seed 0.
SDs describe assignment-draw variation only, not survey sampling or model uncertainty.
The OBR-sized run is a different, smaller shock (1.7% displacement, no wage or capital channel), not a step on the central ladder.
Regional results are not on the study's data/microcosm-2024-25 branch; results/geo/ exists only on main and predates the move to Microcosm (FRS-era, superseded).

absolute_bhc_pct.note: Baseline (no shock), FY 2026-27; the baseline does not depend on the draw.

channels.note: Each channel run alone on the same 20 draws (seeds 0-19) as the central case.

cost_components.key: <component>.mean and .sd; positive = cost to the Exchequer (fall in gov_balance)

rows.label: Income tax on earnings, net of tax on survivors' wage gains

wage.key: zero crossing of exchequer_cost_bn over survivor_wage_effect_pct (seed 0)

capital.key: linear between mean central cost (results/robustness/dividend_coverage_draws.csv run=central) at the central uplift and mean cost of variant cap60 at +60%, seeds 0-19

duration.key: 12 x (1 - r), r = 0.5 full / (full - half); full = mean results/robustness/incidence_draws_five.csv family=exposure seeds 0-19, half = half_earnings_retention.results.exchequer_cost_bn.mean

breakeven.note: Each value sets the central cost to zero with the other two at their central settings (linear interpolation). Full take-up and new-style JSA move each further away.

job_loss.key: mean(exchequer_cost_bn) of run=channel_displacement over mean(gross_cut_bn) of results/wage_cut/wage_cut_draws.csv variant=cut_only, seeds 0-19; min/max of the per-draw ratio

per_pound_20.note: Displacement alone and wage cuts alone: no survivor-wage or capital channel in either.

sankey.key: per decile: earnings lost = -market_change; lower income tax and employee NI = -tax_change; more benefits = benefit_change; lower disposable income = -net_income_change; other items = the remainder
sankey.note: OBR-sized run: 1.67% of employees displaced under exposure-proportional incidence, survivors' earnings flat, no capital shock; by baseline decile of equivalised HBAI income. Other items are mainly pension contributions, plus council tax and other deductions inside the HBAI concept.

rankings.label: HBAI, leaving out households with large pension contributions

policy.key: mean and SD over seeds of exchequer_cost_bn, poverty_change_bhc_pp, gini_change_pp per reform and family

rows.label: Wage insurance: half of lost earnings, up to £15,000 a year
Benefit cap suspended and UC taper cut from 55% to 45%

policy.note: Each reform is simulated on top of the central shock (shocked-plus-reform minus shocked, poverty lines at their shocked values). Wage insurance is a post-simulation transfer, untaxed and ignored by means tests, so its cost is gross; the two UC reforms are parameter changes, so their costs are net of withdrawal elsewhere. The designs differ in aim and administration.
